## Verdict

**Inkwell** costs least for a team of 22, at **$242 per month**. Its $11 per-seat rate is the lowest on the list, and its 20-seat minimum sits below the team size, so all 22 seats are billed at list with nothing wasted. Dorado is next at $528; Borealis is dearest at $600, since its 40-seat minimum forces payment for 18 seats the team will not use.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $24 | 5 |
| Inkwell | $11 | 20 |
| Borealis | $15 | 40 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 22 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Inkwell:** minimum 20 < 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $11 = **$242 per month**. Effective rate $11.00 per person.
- **Dorado:** minimum 5 < 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $24 = **$528 per month**. Effective rate $24.00 per person.
- **Borealis:** minimum 40 > 22, so 40 seats paid. 40 × $15 = **$600 per month**. Effective rate $27.27 per person ($600 ÷ 22); 18 seats worth $270 go unused.

Inkwell is $286 per month cheaper than Dorado and $358 per month cheaper than Borealis — $3,432 and $4,296 respectively over twelve months.

## Risks

Borealis's position is a minimum-seat artefact. Its $600 is fixed until headcount reaches 40, at which point its effective rate drops to the list $15 — still above Inkwell's $11, so Inkwell leads on list price at every size at or above 20 seats. Dorado never overtakes Inkwell on rate, but it is the cheapest option below 20 people, where Inkwell's floor bills a flat $220.

This comparison covers list price only. The price list carries no information on features, support tiers, usage limits, or security posture, so a cheaper seat may buy less product — that gap is unmeasured here.

All figures assume monthly billing at list, as stated. Annual commitments, volume discounts, onboarding fees, and migration costs are not in the source and could reorder these results.
